section_title: Cased Hole: Cement Evaluation & Casing Integrity
image_source: User-selected four-panel composite, separated by lossless image cropping
engineering_status: Not approved; must be verified against actual MIT mechanics and geometry

shots.title: Entering the Cased World
shots.screen: upper casing and casing shoe visible, with rough open hole below
shots.purpose: Make the transition into an already-cased interval physically readable; after drilling a deeper section, the complete BHA travels upward into existing casing.
shots.audience: We are moving from exposed rock into an existing steel-lined section of the well.

shots.title: What Lies Behind Steel
shots.screen: side-on and slightly deviated casing, same tool with sensing region visible
shots.purpose: Show ultrasonic casing response varies with what supports steel immediately behind it, contrasting better-bonded cement and a fluid/poor-support condition.
shots.audience: Even though cement is hidden by steel, differences in acoustic ringing can offer clues about support behind the casing.

shots.title: The Hidden Channel
shots.screen: longitudinal casing, selectively translucent outside showing a localized axial fluid channel in the cement annulus
shots.purpose: Reveal the spatial location and axial continuity of a possible cement-free, fluid-filled path on one side of casing.
shots.audience: The issue is not necessarily uniform around the pipe; a narrow channel can persist along one side of the casing.

shots.title: The Damage Within
shots.screen: inside steel casing at an oblique grazing angle with ECCO on left and a local inner-wall wear groove on right
shots.purpose: Reveal internal casing metal loss as a local increase in the measured inner radius, not an outside fracture or rock cavity.
shots.audience: The tool can help measure a local change in the inside shape of casing, indicating wear.
